evidence.red_green: Reverted latch (`if not self._degraded and len(self._pending_streak) >= DEGRADATION_THRESHOLD` -> `if False and ...`) => `1 failed, 1 passed, 10 deselected in 6.02s`; AssertionError: 3rd consecutive distinct empty must latch / assert False is True. Latch restored => `2 passed, 10 deselected in 7.51s`. Verbatim text is pasted into the degradation test docstring.

probe_rapid.note: 4/4 identical forced queries (force=True, bypassing the negative cache) returned 0 results with ok=True, latencies 2.0-2.6ms; unresponsive_engines stayed []. By contrast every answered request took 172-948ms. Zero-result pages return faster than any real search can run, so latency is a second, independent degradation signal.

budget.breakdown: 1 curl field-probe (sandboxing LLM agents survey) + 7 distinct client queries + 4 rapid identical forced queries
budget.pace: min_interval_s=1.5, jitter_s=0.5, max_attempts=1 (one HTTP request per query)

observed_fields.notes: Result objects are sparse and conditional: duckduckgo hits carried no `engine`, `engines` or `score`; several carried `publishedDate: null` and `pubdate: ''`; bing hits carried engine='bing', engines=['bing'], score=1.0. Parser accepts `content` (primary) then `snippet`, and `publishedDate` then `published_date` then `pubdate`, falling back to the requested engine when `engine` is absent. Full key set seen: title, url, content, engine, engines, score, publishedDate, pubdate, parsed_url, category, template, positions, priority, thumbnail, img_src, iframe_src, audio_src, length, author, metadata, views, open_group, close_group. Envelope keys: query, results, answers, corrections, infoboxes, suggestions, unresponsive_engines. NOTE: `unresponsive_engines` was [] on every empty response - the service does not self-report the failure.

commands: sed-style revert of the degradation latch + pytest -k degradation (red), restore, pytest -k degradation (green)
